failures.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
failures.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase: noted on a nightly card, drafted when its count how often it fires, registered once you say yes, tested on 2000-2023 only at a the strict pass mark, then run as a paper trial on live sessions (20 recorded). Only if it beats the random picks and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs, passes the check that no future data leaked in, and you say yes again is it admitted, which is the first point where allocated paper capital may use it. After that comes the final real-money gate, which needs the India gate and your yes. Right now no rule has been admitted: the stock rules are in the paper-trial step and have beaten chance on 6 of the 10 days needed, and the options line has 9 of its 20 sessions.

problems.why: It uses 'staircase' and an unexplained 'India gate', plus garbled phrasing ('when its count how often it fires', 'at a the strict pass mark') and unclear figures ('20 recorded', '6 of the 10 days'), which a beginner could not follow.

results.text: I want to know what's in detail.
results.answer: It is Thursday 5 Nov, 19:07 in India (Thursday 5 Nov, 8:37 am in Toronto): today's NSE session has CLOSED (it closed at 15:30 IST), 3 h 37 min ago. Sir, the session is closed, so here is the why behind it. Why it rose: both indexes opened with big gaps up (Nifty +1.7%, Bank Nifty +2.1%) and kept climbing from there. Foreign institutions bought and domestic institutions sold about ₹10,445 crore, so foreigners did the lifting. Ananta found no company filing behind the day's moves, so I would call it a market-wide move, not news on one stock. Why the options line took Bank Nifty: at 09:15 its model predicted a further fall of about 43 points. Costs are about 34 points, which left 9 points, just above its bar of 7. Bank Nifty's bar is deliberately loose, so a thin edge is enough. Why it passed on Nifty: its best predicted gain after costs was below zero at all four checks (09:15, 09:30, 09:45, 10:15), and Nifty's bar is five times stricter. It does not look at the option's price when it decides. What went wrong: the model expected a fall after a big gap up and the market kept rising. It is one lot and one session, and the options line has 9 of 20 sessions on record, so this proves nothing yet. Your holdings: TMCV rose 6.5% and TMPV 5.5%, both on heavy volume (4x and 2x their usual). JIOFIN rose 3.3%. UNITDSPR fell 1.8% and MARICO 0.2%. The managed book planned 0 cuts and 0 buys, so it did nothing; its official result is booked in the evening run. Next: on Friday 6 Nov the options line decides again between 09:15 and 10:15 IST. The US jobs report comes out at 19:00 IST that day, which is after the Indian close.

results.answer: Yes, sir, I understand: you mean the market's phase over weeks (up, down, or ranging before a break) rather than tomorrow's single move. Ananta tested this on the Nifty for 2003-2023. Quiet range days were followed by bigger moves, so they say how much the market may move, not which way, and a narrowing range stopped working after 2018.
